settings.heading: Fashion without the footprint
settings.text: Making a brand-new garment takes land, water, energy and labour. The most sustainable piece in your wardrobe is the one that already exists. That is the whole idea behind our store.

settings.heading: Too many good clothes end up in landfill.
settings.text: Most of New Zealand's discarded clothing is still wearable. We give it somewhere better to go.

settings.title: Source locally
settings.text: Pieces come from Auckland closets and clear-outs, with no overseas shipping of stock.

settings.title: Clean & repair
settings.text: Items are washed and given small repairs, such as a new button or a mended seam, before listing.

settings.title: Pack with care
settings.text: Recycled paper mailers, paper tape and recycled-card labels. Nothing plastic.

settings.title: Close the loop
settings.text: Customers can return pieces for store credit, so garments keep circulating.

settings.question: Is buying second-hand really more sustainable?
settings.answer: Yes. Every garment you buy pre-loved is one that does not need to be made from scratch, and one that does not go to landfill. Wearing a piece for longer is one of the most effective ways to lower its environmental impact.

settings.question: How do you grade condition?
settings.answer: Like new: worn once or twice, no visible wear. Excellent: lightly worn with minor signs of use only. Good: clearly worn but sound; any flaws are listed on the product page.

settings.question: What happens to items you cannot sell?
settings.answer: Unsold pieces are donated to local charity shops or passed on to a textile recycler. We aim for nothing to go to landfill.

settings.heading: Pass your good clothes on
settings.text: Send us the pieces you no longer wear and earn store credit.
